signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono {q k s : ℝ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqk : q ≤ k) (hks : k < s - 1) :
  q / (s - q - 1) ≤ k / (s - k - 1)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono
doc:
Monotonicity of the completion factor (Chen–Persson, proof of `thm:GN`): `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
is increasing for `q < s − 1`, so the factor of `lem:completion` for dimension `q ≤ k` is at
most that for `k`. Helper for atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X Y cfac : Ω → ℝ}
  {cmax B : ℝ} (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hcmax : 0 ≤ cmax) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ cmax)
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hYbound : ∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ ≤ B)
  (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ) (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ cmax * B
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly
doc:
Abstract assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Y = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` (the range-finder error),
  `cfac ω = 1 + q(ω)/(s − q(ω) − 1)` with `q = rank(AΩ)` the (random) number of columns of `Q`.
* `hcond` encodes `lem:completion` after the tower property (conditioning on `Ω`, using
  independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`): `E X = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) Y]`.
* `hc` is the deterministic bound `q ≤ t` and monotonicity of `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
  (`completion_factor_mono`).
* `hYbound` is the range-finder theorem (`thm:RSVD`).
Atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Y cfac Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {k t s OPTsq : ℝ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t)
  (hts : t + 2 ≤ s) (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ 1 + t / (s - t - 1))
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hstruct : ∀ (ω : Ω), Y ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = k / (t - k - 1) * OPTsq) (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ)
  (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + t / (s - t - 1)) * ((1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * OPTsq)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit
doc:
Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1), expectation level:
`t ≥ k+2`, `s ≥ t+2`,
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Hypotheses: `hc` (`lem:completion`'s factor with `q = rank(AΩ) ≤ t`), `hcond`
(`lem:completion` + tower property), `hstruct` (`prop:hmt-struct` for
`Y = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F²`), `hZ` (`lem:moments` + `lem:invmom`, as in the proof of `thm:RSVD`).
The hypothesis `hk` is not used by the arithmetic; it is kept for fidelity.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (uses `rsvd-expected-error`).

name: NLAlib.Assembly.integral_le_sqrt_integral_sq
doc:
Jensen's inequality in the form used throughout Chen–Persson: for a nonnegative
square-integrable random variable `Y`, `E Y ≤ √(E Y²)`. Proved from
`0 ≤ Var Y = E Y² − (E Y)²`. Helper for atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (Frobenius-norm,
unsquared form of HMT 2011, Thm 10.5).

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.rsvd_assembly.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {OPTsq c : ℝ} (hX : ∀ (ω : Ω), X ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = c * OPTsq) (hXi : MeasureTheory.Integrable X μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + c) * OPTsq
name: NLAlib.Assembly.rsvd_assembly
doc:
Assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` (HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Zsq = ‖Σ₂ Ω₂ Ω₁†‖_F²`, `OPTsq = ‖Σ₂‖_F² = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD
doc:
`IsSVD A U V`: `U`, `V` are orthogonal and `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1). The `k`-th columns of `U` and `V` are the
left/right singular vectors for `σ_k`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.apply

Thin-SVD / outer-product expansion, entrywise:
`A i j = ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k U_{ik} V_{jk}`, i.e. `A = ∑_k σ_k u_k v_kᵀ`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs : n → ℝ) : (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error `E‖x_k - xs‖²` after `k` randomized Kaczmarz steps started at `x`,
rows drawn i.i.d. with probabilities `prob A`. Defined by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x - xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ i, prob A i * expErr k (step A b x i)`.
See `expErr_eq_sum_paths` for the path-sum form. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k =
    ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths
doc:
`expErr` is the expectation over i.i.d. row sequences: the sum over all `ω : Fin k → m` of
`(∏ j, prob A (ω j)) * ‖run A b k ω x - xs‖²`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation.**
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
If `A *ᵥ xs = b` and `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`, then after `k` steps with rows drawn
i.i.d. with probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ - xs‖²`.
Deviations from the printed statement: SV09 take `A` of full column rank and `σ = ‖A⁻¹‖⁻¹`
(rate `1 - κ(A)⁻²`); here `σ` is any constant satisfying `hσ` (the sharp choice is
`σ_min(A)`, atlas `courant-fischer`), and no rank or nonzero-row assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x (k + 1) =
    ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i) k
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `k + 1` steps (first-step analysis). Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x 0 = (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `0` steps. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (hA : A ≠ 0) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity:
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - ‖A (x - xs)‖² / ‖A‖_F²` for `A ≠ 0`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le
doc:
One-step contraction of randomized Kaczmarz: if `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`
(`σ` a lower bound on the smallest singular value, atlas `courant-fischer`), then
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²) ‖x - xs‖²`.
No hypothesis on `A` (for `A = 0` the left side is `0` and the rate is `1`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (i : m) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob
doc:
Row-selection probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²` of randomized Kaczmarz.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (i : m) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg
doc: Selection probabilities are nonnegative. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.rate_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Nonempty n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  0 ≤ 1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.rate_nonneg
doc:
The contraction factor is nonnegative when `n` is nonempty: `σ² ≤ ‖A‖_F²`.
Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (Fin k → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run
doc:
The iterate after applying the steps with rows `ω 0, ω 1, …, ω (k-1)` in that order,
starting from `x`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x✝ : ℕ)
  (x✝¹ : Fin x✝ → m) (x✝² : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b x✝ x✝¹ x✝² =
    match (motive := (x : ℕ) → (Fin x → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ) x✝, x✝¹, x✝² with
    | 0, x, x_1 => x_1
    | k.succ, ω, x => NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k (Fin.tail ω) (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x (ω 0))
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) ^ 2 / A i ⬝ᵥ A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step
doc:
Pythagoras for one Kaczmarz step (the step is an orthogonal projection onto a hyperplane
containing `xs`): `‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs))² / ‖A i‖²`.
Holds for every row; for a zero row both sides equal `‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ)
  (i : m) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step
doc:
One Kaczmarz step on row `i`: the orthogonal projection of `x` onto the hyperplane
`{y | A i ⬝ᵥ y = b i}`. For a zero row the step is the identity (real division by zero is `0`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm (eq. (2)); atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs = x - xs - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) / A i ⬝ᵥ A i) • A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution
doc:
Error recursion of one Kaczmarz step when `A *ᵥ xs = b`:
`step A b x i - xs = (x - xs) - ((A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) / ‖A i‖²) • A i`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_paths_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) *
        (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_paths_le
doc:
Path-sum form of SV09 Thm 2: the weighted average over all row sequences of length `k` of
the squared error is at most `(1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_prob.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (hA : A ≠ 0) : ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i = 1
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_prob
doc: The selection probabilities sum to one when `A ≠ 0`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature: NLAlib.LoewnerLE.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] (A B : Matrix d d ℂ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.LoewnerLE
doc:
The Loewner (semidefinite) order: `LoewnerLE A B` iff `B - A` is positive semidefinite. Tropp
2015, §2.1.5. Atlas: `loewner-order`.

signature: NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn (I : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn
doc:
`f` is operator convex on the convex set `I`: `f (t A + (1-t) H) ≼ t f(A) + (1-t) f(H)` for all
Hermitian `A`, `H` of every size with spectra in `I`. Tropp 2015, Def. 8.4.6. Atlas:
`operator-monotone-convex`.

signature:
NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn.matrixFunction_conjTranspose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ] (I : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (hf : NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn I f) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAI : spectrum ℝ A ⊆ I) (K : Matrix ι κ ℂ)
  (hK : K.conjTranspose * K = 1) :
  NLAlib.LoewnerLE (NLAlib.matrixFunction f (K.conjTranspose * A * K)) (K.conjTranspose * NLAlib.matrixFunction f A * K)
name: NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn.matrixFunction_conjTranspose_mul_mul_le
doc:
Operator Jensen inequality for an isometry: if `f` is operator convex on `I` and `Kᴴ K = 1`, then
`f (Kᴴ A K) ≼ Kᴴ f(A) K`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 8.5.2 (single-isometry form). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from the
Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_add_mul_log_add_le (a δ : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1) :

name: NLAlib.abs_add_mul_log_add_le
doc:
`|(a + δ) log (a + δ)| ≤ |a log a| + a + 2` for `a ≥ 0` and `0 < δ ≤ 1`. Atlas:
`gaussian-log-sobolev` (helper). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_logsobolev`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_apply_le_apply_self_add_apply_self.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (M : Matrix m m ℝ)
  (hM : M.PosSemidef) (i j : m) : |M i j| ≤ M i i + M j j
name: NLAlib.abs_apply_le_apply_self_add_apply_self
doc:
An entry of a real positive semidefinite matrix is dominated by the diagonal:
`|Mᵢⱼ| ≤ Mᵢᵢ + Mⱼⱼ`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, App. B. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Ported from the
Prove2me solution `Sol_GaussianMatrix_inverse_wishart_rotation_relation` (`iwr_psd_offdiag`).

signature:
NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_mulVec_le_specNorm.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (M : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : |x ⬝ᵥ M.mulVec x| ≤ NLAlib.specNorm M * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.abs_dotProduct_mulVec_le_specNorm
doc:
Quadratic-form bound by the spectral norm: `|xᵀ M x| ≤ ‖M‖₂ ‖x‖²`. Helper for the Gram form
of `ose-def`; atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

signature: NLAlib.abs_eval_U_real_le {x : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 1) (q : ℕ) : |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.U ℝ ↑q)| ≤ ↑q + 1
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_U_real_le
doc:
The Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind is bounded by `q + 1` on `[-1, 1]`:
`|x| ≤ 1 → |U_q(x)| ≤ q + 1`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), §1.5. Atlas: `chebyshev-second-kind`. Proof: `T_{q+1}' = (q + 1) U_q`
and Mathlib's `abs_iterate_derivative_T_real_le` with one derivative.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevAmplifier_le {α γ x : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (hα : 0 < α) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-α) α) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q)| ≤ 2 / (1 + √(2 * γ)) ^ q
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevAmplifier_le
doc:
On `[−α, α]` the amplifier is exponentially small: `|p(x)| ≤ 2/(1 + √(2γ))^q`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4; Lem. 5 is the case `γ = ε`. Atlas:
`chebyshev-amplifier`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevResidual_le {a b x : ℝ} {q : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q)| ≤
    1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevResidual_le
doc:
On `[a, b]` with `0 < a < b`, the residual polynomial is at most
`1 / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))` in modulus.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevResidual_le_two_mul_pow {a b x : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q)| ≤ 2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_chebyshevResidual_le_two_mul_pow
doc:
κ-form of the Chebyshev residual bound: for `0 < a < b` and `x ∈ [a, b]`,
`|chebyshevResidual a b q (x)| ≤ 2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8; Trefethen–Bau (1997), Thm 38.5. Atlas:
`chebyshev-minimax` (κ-form).

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_T_real_le {x : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 1) (q : ℕ) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q))| ≤ ↑q ^ 2
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_T_real_le
doc:
The derivative of `T_q` is bounded by `q²` on `[-1, 1]`: `|x| ≤ 1 → |T_q'(x)| ≤ q²`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), §1.5 (the case `p = T_q` of Markov's inequality). Atlas:
`chebyshev-second-kind`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : |x| < 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q * M / √(1 - x ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Bernstein's inequality** for algebraic polynomials. If `p` has degree at most `q` and
`|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q M / √(1 − x²)` for `|x| < 1`.

Source: Bernstein (1912); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7; Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
Proof (algebraic form of the trigonometric argument): with `a = x = cos θ₀`, `b = √(1 − x²)`, the
odd part of `θ ↦ p(cos(θ₀ + θ))` is `sin θ · r(cos θ)` for a polynomial `r` of degree `< q` (built
from Hasse derivatives of `p`), `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, and `r(1) = −b p'(x)`; Schur's
inequality `abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` at `y = 1` gives
`b |p'(x)| ≤ q M`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q ^ 2 * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality** (the first Markov inequality, sharp constant). If `p` has
degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q² M` for all `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), Thm 2.24 / §2.7;
Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
Proof: Bernstein's inequality `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le` gives
`√(1 − y²) |p'(y)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`, and Schur's inequality
`abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` applied to `p'` (degree `< q`) gives
`|p'(x)| ≤ q · q M`. The equality case (`p = ±M T_q`, `x = ±1`) is not formalised.

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality on an interval.** If `p` has degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on
`[a, b]` (`a < b`), then `|p'(x)| ≤ 2 q² / (b − a) · M` for all `x ∈ [a, b]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (affine
rescaling of `abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`). Atlas: `markov-brothers`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_inv_two_pow_mul_T_le {q : ℕ} {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.C (1 / 2 ^ (q - 1)) * Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)| ≤ 1 / 2 ^ (q - 1)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_inv_two_pow_mul_T_le
doc:
The scaled Chebyshev polynomial `2^(1−q) T_q` is at most `1 / 2^(q−1)` in modulus on
`[−1, 1]`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le_one {q : ℕ} {P : Polynomial ℝ} {x : ℝ} (hP : P.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hb : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ 1) (hx : 1 ≤ |x|) :
  |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)|
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le_one
doc:
Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and `|P| ≤ 1` on `[−1, 1]`,
then `|P(x)| ≤ |T_q(x)|` for every `|x| ≥ 1`.
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Thm 2.20 (case `k = 0`); Mathlib
`Polynomial.Chebyshev.eval_iterate_derivative_le_of_forall_abs_le_one` covers `x ≥ 1`;
Atlas: `chebyshev-extremal`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le {q : ℕ} {P : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hP : P.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hb : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ M) (hx : 1 ≤ |x|) :
  |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ M * |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)|
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le
doc:
Scaled form of Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and
`|P| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|P(x)| ≤ M |T_q(x)|` for every `|x| ≥ 1`. No sign condition on `M`
(for `M ≤ 0` the hypothesis forces `P = 0`).
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Thm 2.20 (case `k = 0`);
Atlas: `chebyshev-extremal`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {r : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q)
  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, √(1 - y ^ 2) * |Polynomial.eval y r| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x r| ≤ ↑q * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Schur's inequality.** If `r` has degree `< q` and `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then
`|r(x)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`.

Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (Schur's lemma); Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Proof: for `|x| ≤ cos(π/(2q))` directly from
`√(1 − x²) ≥ sin(π/(2q)) ≥ 1/q`; for `x ≥ cos(π/(2q))` by Lagrange interpolation at the zeros
`ξ_k` of `T_q`, where all partial nodal products are nonnegative and the weights satisfy
`|r(ξ_k)| / |T_q'(ξ_k)| ≤ M/q`, so `|r(x)| ≤ (M/q) T_q'(x) ≤ q M`; the case `x ≤ −cos(π/(2q))` by
reflection. Atlas: auxiliary for `markov-brothers` and `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_nodal_chebyshevZero_le (q : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ (NLAlib.chebyshevZero q))| ≤ 1 / 2 ^ (q - 1)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_nodal_chebyshevZero_le
doc:
On `[−1, 1]` the nodal polynomial of the `q` Chebyshev zeros is at most `1/2^(q−1)` in
modulus. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Ch. 3; Cheney, Ch. 3. Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`
(lemma). Deviation: no `0 < q` hypothesis.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_frobInner_le_frobNorm_mul_frobNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) : |NLAlib.frobInner A B| ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm A * NLAlib.frobNorm B
name: NLAlib.abs_frobInner_le_frobNorm_mul_frobNorm
doc: Cauchy–Schwarz, absolute-value form: `|⟨A, B⟩_F| ≤ ‖A‖_F ‖B‖_F`. Atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_le_abs_add_mul_abs_of_abs_deriv_le (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (C : ℝ)
  (hdf : ∀ (x : ℝ), |deriv f x| ≤ C) (z : ℝ) : |f z| ≤ |f 0| + C * |z|
name: NLAlib.abs_le_abs_add_mul_abs_of_abs_deriv_le
doc:
A function with derivative bounded by `C` grows at most linearly:
`|f z| ≤ |f 0| + C |z|`. Atlas: `gaussian-integration-by-parts` (helper). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.gaussian_ibp_one_dim`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_le_norm_of_mem_spectrum.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] [Nonempty d] (B : Matrix d d ℂ)
  {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ spectrum ℝ B) : |x| ≤ ‖B‖
name: NLAlib.abs_le_norm_of_mem_spectrum
doc:
A real spectral value of a square complex matrix is bounded in absolute value by its ℓ₂
operator norm. Tropp 2015, §2.1.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_sub_eval_interpolate_chebyshevZero_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {M : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo (-1) 1))

      M / (2 ^ q * ↑(q + 1).factorial)

`f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(−1, 1)` and `|f^{(q+1)}| ≤ M` on `(−1, 1)`. The polynomial
interpolating `f` at the `q + 1` zeros of `T_{q+1}` satisfies
`|f x − L(x)| ≤ M / (2^q (q + 1)!)` for every `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Approximation Practice*, Ch. 11; Cheney, Ch. 3.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`; uses `interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: the derivative bound is assumed only on the open interval `(−1, 1)` (weaker than
on `[−1, 1]`).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
The gap-amplifying polynomial `chebyshevAmplifier α γ q = T_q(X/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`: equal to
`1` at `α(1 + γ)`, increasing beyond it, and exponentially small on `[−α, α]`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5; Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C (1 / α) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual
doc:

`chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2 X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`. For `0 < a < b`
it has the smallest maximum modulus on `[a, b]` among polynomials of degree at most `q` with
value `1` at `0` (the residual polynomial of Chebyshev iteration and the model for CG).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C ((b + a) / (b - a)) - Polynomial.C (2 / (b - a)) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def

          (NLAlib.pinvL ((Ψ ω).transpose * Q) * ((Ψ ω).transpose * Qp) * (Qp.transpose * NLAlib.residual Q A)))
      μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - NLAlib.sketchedOutput Q (Ψ ω) A) ∂μ =
    (1 + ↑q / (↑s - ↑q - 1)) * NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.residual Q A)
name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = residual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).

doc:
**Gross's Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality** in dimension one: for `g ∈ C¹` with
`g², g² log g², g'² ∈ L¹(γ)`,
`∫ g² log g² dγ - (∫ g² dγ) log ∫ g² dγ ≤ 2 ∫ g'² dγ`.
Source: Gross 1975, Thm 5; Ledoux, *Concentration of Measure*, Thm 5.1 (`n = 1`). Atlas:
`gaussian-log-sobolev`. Ported from Prove2me solution

doc:

`∫ g² log g² dγ - (∫ g² dγ) log ∫ g² dγ ≤ 2 ∫ g'² dγ`.

`gaussian-log-sobolev`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_logsobolev_one_dim_compact_support`.

signature:
NLAlib.entropy_sq_le_two_mul_integral_sum_sq_fderiv_gaussian.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)) :
  (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) -

signature:

doc:
The Chebyshev zeros are roots of `T_q`.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error` (API).

signature:
NLAlib.eval_T_real_eq_of_one_le {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (q : ℕ) :
  Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) = ((x + √(x ^ 2 - 1)) ^ q + (x - √(x ^ 2 - 1)) ^ q) / 2
name: NLAlib.eval_T_real_eq_of_one_le
doc:
Closed form of `T_q` on `[1, ∞)`: for `1 ≤ x`,
`T_q(x) = ((x + √(x² − 1))^q + (x − √(x² − 1))^q)/2`.
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Eq. (1.49); Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], proof
of Lem. 4. Atlas: `chebyshev-growth`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_T_real_le_pow {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (q : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.eval_T_real_le_pow
doc:
Upper bound on the growth of `T_q` on `[1, ∞)`: for `1 ≤ x`, `T_q(x) ≤ (x + √(x² − 1))^q`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), §1.5. Atlas: `chebyshev-growth`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q) =
    Polynomial.eval (x / α) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.eval_chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
`chebyshevAmplifier α γ q` at `x` is `T_q(x/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4. Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_chebyshevAmplifier_self {α γ : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (hα : 0 < α) (hγ : 0 ≤ γ) :
  Polynomial.eval (α * (1 + γ)) (NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q) = 1
name: NLAlib.eval_chebyshevAmplifier_self
doc:
The amplifier equals `1` at `α(1 + γ)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4. Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q) =
    Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a) - 2 / (b - a) * x) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) /
      Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.eval_chebyshevResidual
doc:
`chebyshevResidual a b q` at `x` is `T_q((b + a − 2x)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`.
Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_chebyshevResidual_zero {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) :
  Polynomial.eval 0 (NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q) = 1
name: NLAlib.eval_chebyshevResidual_zero
doc:
The residual polynomial `chebyshevResidual a b q` has value `1` at `0`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_derivative_T_real_one (q : ℕ) :

The derivative of `T_q` at `1` is `q²`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), §1.5; Mathlib `T_derivative_eq_U` and `U_eval_one`. Atlas:
`chebyshev-second-kind`.

signature:
NLAlib.eval_iterate_derivative_natDegree (p : Polynomial ℝ) (x : ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.eval_iterate_derivative_natDegree
doc: The `n`-th derivative of a polynomial of degree `n` is the constant `n! · leadingCoeff`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_contDiff_abs_sub_le_of_lipschitz.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ g,
    (∀ (n : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ (↑n) g) ∧
      (∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |g x - g y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) ∧ ∀ (x : ι → ℝ), |g x - f x| ≤ ε
name: NLAlib.exists_contDiff_abs_sub_le_of_lipschitz
doc:
**Smooth approximation of Lipschitz functions**: an `L`-Lipschitz (Euclidean) function
`f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ` is within `ε` of a `C^∞` function that is again `L`-Lipschitz (mollify with a
normed bump of small support). Source: standard; Ledoux, *Concentration of Measure*, §5.1.
Atlas: `gaussian-concentration` (helper). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.lipschitz_smooth_approx`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le {a b : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) :
  ∃ p, p.degree < ↑q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, |Polynomial.eval x p - 1 / x| ≤ 2 / a * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le
doc:
Polynomial approximation of `1/x` on `[a, b]`: for `0 < a < b` there is a polynomial `p` of
degree `< q` with `|p(x) − 1/x| ≤ (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q` on `[a, b]`. The polynomial is
`p = (1 − r)/X` for the Chebyshev residual `r = chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the CG error bound). Atlas:
`inverse-polynomial-approx`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iInf_sqrt_mulVec_le_of_sigmaMin_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (s : ℝ) (hs : NLAlib.sigmaMin A ≤ s) :
  ∃ j, ⨅ x, √(A.mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec ↑x) ≤ √↑(Fintype.card n) * s
name: NLAlib.exists_iInf_sqrt_mulVec_le_of_sigmaMin_le
doc:
**Small `σ_min` forces a column close to the span of the others.** For `A : Matrix m n ℝ`
with `n` nonempty, if `σ_min(A) ≤ s` then for some column `j`,
`inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 } ≤ √|n| · s`; the left side is the distance from column `j` to the
span of the other columns.

Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Rudelson–Vershynin 2008, Lemma 3.5 (the
"invertibility via distance" step). Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Generalised from
`Fin N × Fin n` (with `1 ≤ n`) to arbitrary finite index types with `n` nonempty. Ported from
Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.sMin_le_imp_dist_le`.

signature: NLAlib.exists_isSVD {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ U V, NLAlib.IsSVD A U V
name: NLAlib.exists_isSVD
doc:
**Singular value decomposition** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1): every real
`m × n` matrix is `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `U`, `V` orthogonal and `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`,
the singular values being nonnegative and non-increasing (`singularValues_nonneg`,
`singularValues_antitone`). Atlas `svd`.

Proof: `V` is an orthonormal eigenbasis of `AᵀA` (Mathlib's spectral theorem, sorted), the
vectors `A vⱼ / σⱼ` with `σⱼ ≠ 0` are orthonormal and are completed to an orthonormal basis of
`ℝᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {s : Finset ℝ} (hs : s.card = q + 2)
  (hsab : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem**, finset form: if `f` vanishes on a set of `q + 2` points of
`[a, b]` (hypotheses as in `exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono`), then `f^{(q+1)}`
vanishes somewhere in `(a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, proof of Thm 6.2. Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 2) → ℝ}
  (hv : StrictMono v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), f (v i) = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem.** If `f` vanishes at `q + 2` points `v 0 < ⋯ < v (q+1)` of
`[a, b]`, `f` is continuous on `[a, b]` and the derivatives `f', …, f^{(q)}` are continuous on
`(a, b)`, then `f^{(q+1)}(ξ) = 0` for some `ξ ∈ (a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, proof of Thm 6.2; Atkinson,
*An Introduction to Numerical Analysis* (2nd ed.), proof of Thm 3.2.
Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
Deviation: stated with `q + 2` zeros and the `(q + 1)`-st derivative (so the conclusion is in the
open interval without a side condition); only continuity of `f^{(k)}`, `1 ≤ k ≤ q`, on `(a, b)`
is assumed — no differentiability, because `iteratedDeriv` is Mathlib's global derivative and
Rolle (`exists_deriv_eq_zero`) needs only continuity.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_completion.{u_4} {k : ℕ} {ι : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (V : Matrix (Fin k) ι ℝ)
  (hV : V.transpose * V = 1) (e : ι ↪ Fin k) : ∃ W, W.transpose * W = 1 ∧ ∀ (i : Fin k) (j : ι), W i (e j) = V i j
name: NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_completion
doc:
**Orthogonal completion.** A real matrix `V` with orthonormal columns indexed by `ι`, placed
in the columns `e '' ι` of `Fin k`, extends to an orthogonal `k × k` matrix `W`.
Helper for HMT 2011 §10.2. Ported from the Prove2me workspace (Gaussian Random Matrices
series). Atlas `orthonormal-completion`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_complement {k q : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin q) ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  ∃ r Qp, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qp ∧ Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1
name: NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_complement
doc:
**Orthonormal complement.** A matrix `Q` with orthonormal columns has a complement `Qp` with
orthonormal columns and `QQᵀ + QpQpᵀ = I` (here `Qp` has `k − q` columns). From
`exists_orthogonal_completion`. Atlas `orthonormal-completion`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_ker_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  ∃ V,
    V.transpose * V = 1 ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin (k - n)), (H.mulVec fun l => V l j) = 0) ∧
        ∀ (g : Fin k → ℝ),
          g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g) = ∑ j, V.transpose.mulVec g j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_ker_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Residual in an orthonormal basis of the kernel.** For `H` of full row rank `n`, an
orthonormal basis `V` (`k × (k - n)`, `Vᵀ V = 1`) of `ker H` writes the squared distance from `g`
to the row space of `H` as `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g) = ‖Vᵀ g‖²`; the columns of `V` are
killed by `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5 (law of the residual of a Gaussian
row and its independence from the regression). Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Ported
from the Prove2me solutions `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law` and
`GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep` (the two copies merged, keeping the stronger
statement).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b x : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ} (hab : a < b)
  (hv : Function.Injective v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 1)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo a b)) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
    f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ v) (f ∘ v)) =
      iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ / ↑(q + 1).factorial * Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq
doc:
**Interpolation remainder formula.** Let `v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ` be distinct nodes in
`[a, b]`, `f` continuous on `[a, b]` with `f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(a, b)`, and
`x ∈ [a, b]`. Then for the interpolating polynomial `L = Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)`
and the nodal polynomial `ω = ∏ (X − v i)` there is `ξ ∈ (a, b)` with
`f x − L(x) = f^{(q+1)}(ξ) / (q + 1)! · ω(x)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, Thm 6.2; Atkinson (2nd ed.),
Thm 3.2; Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas:
`interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: `ξ` is in the open interval `(a, b)` (stronger than `[a, b]`), at the cost of the
hypothesis `a < b` (used only when `x` is a node).

signature:
NLAlib.exp_mul_lambdaMax_lambdaMin_le_traceExp_smul {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)

for `θ < 0`.

Tropp 2015, §3.2, eq. (3.2.3). Atlas: `matrix-laplace`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 3*.

`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

    ENNReal.ofReal (4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the Frobenius norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `t ≥ 1`,
`P[‖G†‖_F² > 12 r t/(k-r)] ≤ 4 t^{-(k-r)/2}`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Thm A.6 (used in Prop 10.4; HMT state it as `P[‖Ω₁†‖_F ≥ √(12k/p) t] ≤ 4 t^{-p}`
with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`, the same bound after `t ↦ √t`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.
Proof: each diagonal entry of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹` is `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`
(`gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), whose `L^{(k-r)/2}` norm is at most
`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's

**Chevet's inequality, with integrability.** For `S : a × p`, `T : m × n` and a `p × m`
standard Gaussian matrix `Γ`, `‖S Γ T‖₂` is integrable and
`𝔼 ‖S Γ T‖₂ ≤ ‖S‖₂ ‖T‖_F + ‖S‖_F ‖T‖₂`. Source: HMT 2011, Prop. A.2. Atlas: `chevet`. Ported
from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.chevet`.

name: NLAlib.integrable_and_integral_specNorm_pinvR_gaussianMatrix_le
doc:
**Expectation of the spectral norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `2 ≤ r` and `r + 1 ≤ k`, `‖G†‖` is integrable and
`E‖G†‖ ≤ e√k/(k-r)`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Prop A.4 (`E‖Ω₁†‖ ≤ e√(k+p)/p` with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`). Atlas:
`pinv-spectral-expectation`. Proof: the tail bound `gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le` (atlas
`pinv-spectral-tail`, uses the scaffold (B.5)) integrated by the layer-cake estimate
`integrable_and_integral_le_of_tail_le_rpow` (atlas `tail-integral`). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_spectral_expectation`.

`GaussianMatrix.spectral_second_moment`.

`gaussian-integration-by-parts`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_ibp_one_dim`.

Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.gaussian_integration_by_parts`.

`(U, V₁, …, V_n)` with `𝔼 U = 0` and `G : ℝⁿ → ℝ` bounded with bounded continuous partial
derivatives `G' j = ∂ⱼG`,
`𝔼[U G(V)] = ∑ⱼ Cov(U, Vⱼ) 𝔼[∂ⱼG(V)]`.
Source: Vershynin 2018, Lemma 7.2.3; Talagrand, *Mean Field Models for Spin Glasses*, Lemma
1.3.1. Proof: regress `V` on `U` (`V = c U + W` with `W ⫫ U`), apply the one-dimensional
identity in `U` and integrate over `W`. Atlas: `gaussian-integration-by-parts`. Ported from
Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.gaussian_integration_by_parts`.

signature:
NLAlib.integral_quadForm_eq_trace.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]

doc:

square-integrable, pairwise independent, centred and have unit second moment, then

`𝔼[z_i z_j] = δ_ij` is used); the source states it for Rademacher `z`.

  (hL2 : ∀ (k : Fin N), MeasureTheory.MemLp (X k) 2 μ) (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L)

name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_minimax
doc:
The Chebyshev minimax theorem on `[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`: the least possible bound `M` for
`|p|` on `[a, b]` over polynomials `p` of degree at most `q` with `p(0) = 1` is
`1 / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`, attained by `chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Trefethen–Bau (1997), Thm 38.5;
Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax (q : ℕ) :
  IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M} (1 / 2 ^ (q - 1))
name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax
doc:
The monic Chebyshev minimax theorem: over monic real polynomials of degree `q`, the least
possible bound for `|p|` on `[−1, 1]` is `1 / 2^(q−1)`, attained by `2^(1−q) T_q`.
Source: Trefethen (2013), Thm 2.2 / Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.
Deviation: stated for all `q`, including `q = 0` (where the value is `1`).

signature: NLAlib.isProbabilityMeasure_gaussianMatrix (p m : ℕ) : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m)
name: NLAlib.isProbabilityMeasure_gaussianMatrix
doc: `gaussianMatrix p m` is a probability measure. Atlas: `gaussian-matrix-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthonormal form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7):
for `U` with orthonormal columns, `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` iff
`(1 - ε)‖x‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖x‖²` for every coefficient vector `x`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_mul_right_iff
doc:
Basis independence (Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for invertible `C`, `S` is an `ε`-subspace
embedding for `range U` iff it is one for `range (U C)`. The property depends on the subspace
only.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le
doc:
Gram form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7), the
direction used in practice: for `U` with orthonormal columns, `‖(SU)ᵀ(SU) − I‖₂ ≤ ε` implies
that `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`. (The converse also holds; not yet
formalized.)

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.isometry_reflection_identities.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (K : Matrix ι κ ℂ) (hK : K.conjTranspose * K = 1) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (B : Matrix κ κ ℂ) :
  have U := Matrix.fromBlocks (1 - K * K.conjTranspose) K K.conjTranspose 0;
  U.IsHermitian ∧ U * U = 1 ∧ (U * Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B * U).toBlocks₂₂ = K.conjTranspose * A * K
name: NLAlib.isometry_reflection_identities
doc:
For an isometry `K`, the block matrix `U = fromBlocks (1 - K Kᴴ) K Kᴴ 0` is a Hermitian involution
and the lower-right block of `U (fromBlocks A 0 0 B) U` is `Kᴴ A K`.

Tropp 2015, proof of Thm 8.5.2 (unitary dilation). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from
the Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

signature:
NLAlib.iteratedDeriv_sub_eval_eqOn {f : ℝ → ℝ} {U : Set ℝ} (hU : IsOpen U) (p : Polynomial ℝ) {n : ℕ}
  (hf : ∀ k < n, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) U) (k : ℕ) :
  k ≤ n →
    Set.EqOn (iteratedDeriv k fun t => f t - Polynomial.eval t p)
      (fun t => iteratedDeriv k f t - Polynomial.eval t ((⇑Polynomial.derivative)^[k] p)) U
name: NLAlib.iteratedDeriv_sub_eval_eqOn
doc:
On an open set `U` where `f, f', …, f^{(n−1)}` are differentiable, the `k`-th derivative
(`k ≤ n`) of `f − p` for a polynomial `p` is `f^{(k)} − p^{(k)}`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
SCAFFOLD: jl-distributional.

Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma for the Gaussian sketch (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003,
Lem 2.2; Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for `S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed
`x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deferred: the proof needs rotation invariance of the Gaussian matrix (`‖Gx‖² / ‖x‖²` is
`χ²_k`) and the two Chernoff tails of the chi-square law (atlas `rotation-invariance`,
`chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`), none of which is yet in the library.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`
distorts some pairwise squared distance by more than `1 ± ε` with probability at most `1/2`.

Deviation: the explicit constant `48` (from `(ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ ≤ 12/ε²` and
`log(4N²) ≤ 4 log N` for `N ≥ 2`) is not optimised; Dasgupta–Gupta's constant is `4·(1/2 − ε/3)⁻¹`
at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hk : (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)⁻¹ * Real.log (2 * ↑N ^ 2 / δ) ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal δ
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least
`1 − δ` the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` preserves all pairwise squared distances of
`p : Fin N → ℝⁿ` to within `1 ± ε`.

Deviation: Dasgupta–Gupta take `k ≥ 4 (ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ log N`, aiming at success probability
`1/N`; we state the general-`δ` form with the constant coming from the ordered-pair union bound
in `jl_lemma`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

`gaussian-conditioning`.

signature: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} : MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)
name: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace
doc:
The Borel σ-algebra on complex matrices (for the norm topology), used to state measurability of
random matrices.

This global instance is a deliberate exception to STANDARDS §3, which states measurability of
matrix-valued maps entrywise because Mathlib has no `MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)`. The matrix
concentration development (ported from the Tropp 2015 Prove2me missions) treats random matrices as
`Measurable` maps into a normed space and integrates them as Bochner integrals in the operator
norm; every statement in `NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/` that mentions `Measurable`, `iIndepFun` or
`Integrable` for a matrix-valued map elaborates through this instance, so removing it would mean
restating the whole development. Mathlib declares no competing instance (`Matrix` is a
non-reducible `def`, so the product σ-algebra on `m → n → ℂ` is not found), hence no diamond. It
could be made `scoped`: checked 2026-10-09, wrapping it in `namespace MatrixBorel` as a `scoped
instance` and adding `open scoped NLAlib.MatrixBorel` to the 35 modules under
`Concentration/Matrix/` that import this one (directly or not) builds cleanly, at the price of
every downstream user opening the scope to state the hypotheses of the public theorems.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_bernstein.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (S : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (S k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun S μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.spectralNorm (S k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, S k ω;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω * (S k ω).conjTranspose ∂μ))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), (S k ω).conjTranspose * S k ω ∂μ)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) + L * Real.log (↑m + ↑n) / 3 ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t
name: NLAlib.matrix_bernstein
doc:
Matrix Bernstein inequality, rectangular case: for an independent sum `Z` of centered random `m ×
n` matrices with `‖S k‖ ≤ L`, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n)) + L log (m + n) / 3` and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 6.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X k ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have a := NLAlib.lambdaMin (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  have b := NLAlib.lambdaMax (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  a = NLAlib.lambdaMin (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
    b = NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
      (∀ (θ : ℝ),
          0 < θ →
            (1 - Real.exp (-θ)) / θ * a - L * Real.log ↑d / θ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ∂μ ∧
              ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (Real.exp θ - 1) / θ * b + L * Real.log ↑d / θ) ∧
        (∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 ≤ ε → ε < 1 → (μ {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ≤ (1 - ε) * a}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail d a L ε) ∧
          ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → (μ {ω | (1 + ε) * b ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail d b L ε
name: NLAlib.matrix_chernoff
doc:
Matrix Chernoff inequality: for an independent sum of random positive semidefinite matrices with
`λmax ≤ L`, expectation bounds on `λmin` and `λmax` for every `θ > 0` and the lower and upper
tails `chernoffLowerTail`, `chernoffUpperTail`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1, eqs (5.1.1–6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission
*An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

The expectation bounds are stated for every `θ > 0` before optimisation; degenerate `L = 0`
follows the piecewise tail definitions.

signature:

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (B : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)

  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, B k * (B k).conjTranspose))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, (B k).conjTranspose * B k)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) ∧

signature:
NLAlib.measure_sigmaMin_le_le_gaussianMatrix {N n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hnN : n ≤ N) (s : ℝ)
  (hsd : ↑n * s ^ 2 ≤ ↑N - ↑n + 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix N n) {A | NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of A) ≤ s} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑n * (Real.exp 1 * ↑n * s ^ 2 / (↑N - ↑n + 1)) ^ ((↑N - ↑n + 1) / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sigmaMin_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small-ball estimate for the smallest singular value of a Gaussian matrix.** For an
`N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `1 ≤ n ≤ N` and `n s² ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(σ_min(A) ≤ s) ≤ n · (e n s² / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`. The source's hypothesis
`0 ≤ s` is not needed and is dropped.

Davidson–Szarek 2001, Thm II.13 (small-ball form); Vershynin 2012, §5.2 /
Rudelson–Vershynin 2009 (sharper `(C s √N)^{N-n+1}` form). Union bound over the columns of the
column-distance estimate. Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.sMin_small_ball`.

signature:
NLAlib.measure_sigmaMin_le_sqrt_sub_sqrt_sub_le_gaussianMatrix {N n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 ≤ u) :

    ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-u ^ 2 / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sigmaMin_le_sqrt_sub_sqrt_sub_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Lower tail of the smallest singular value.** For an `N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `G`
with `n ≥ 1` and `u ≥ 0`, `P(σ_min(G) ≤ √N − √n − u) ≤ e^{-u²/2}`.

Vershynin 2012, Cor. 5.35 (lower half); Davidson–Szarek 2001, Thm II.13.
Atlas: `smin-lower-tail`. The source's hypothesis `n ≤ N` is not needed and is dropped
(Gordon's lower bound `√N − √n ≤ 𝔼 σ_min` holds for all `N`). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.sMin_lower_tail`.

signature:
NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal {N p d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
  (hrank : B.rank + d ≤ N) (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hud : u ≤ ↑d) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
      {g | (⨅ c, √((g - B.mulVec c) ⬝ᵥ (g - B.mulVec c))) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / ↑d) ^ (↑d / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal
doc:
**Small ball for the distance to a subspace.** Let `B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ` have
`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,
`P(dist(g, range B)² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`, with `dist(g, range B) = inf_c ‖g - B c‖₂`.

The squared distance dominates the sum of squares of `d` coordinates of `g` in an orthonormal
basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.

signature:
NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix {N n : ℕ} (hnN : n ≤ N) (j : Fin n) (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 ≤ u)

  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix N n) {A | (⨅ x, √((Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ (Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x)) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / (↑N - ↑n + 1)) ^ ((↑N - ↑n + 1) / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small ball for the distance from a column to the span of the others.** For an `N × n`
standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `n ≤ N`, any column `j` and `0 ≤ u ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(dist(A_j, span{A_l : l ≠ j})² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`, the distance
being written `inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 }`.

Condition on the other columns (resample column `j`) and apply the subspace small-ball bound
with `d = N - n + 1`. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.dist_col_span_small_ball`.

signature:
NLAlib.one_add_div_mul_inv_Gamma_rpow_le {p x : ℕ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp18 : p ≤ 18) (hx : 2 * p ≤ x) :
  (1 + 2 * ↑p / (↑x + 1 - 2 * ↑p)) * (1 / Real.Gamma (↑x + 2)) ^ (2 * ↑p / (↑x + 1)) ≤ (Real.exp 1 / ↑x) ^ (2 * p)
name: NLAlib.one_add_div_mul_inv_Gamma_rpow_le
doc:
**Numerical inequality for the inverse Wishart spectral moments.** For integers
`1 ≤ p ≤ 18` and `x ≥ 2p`,
`(1 + 2p/(x+1-2p)) · (1/Γ(x+2))^{2p/(x+1)} ≤ (e/x)^{2p}`.

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.8) (the range `p ≤ 18` is where the integer check
`(2p+1)^{2p+2} ≤ 46^{2p} ≤ (2π e²)^{2p}` holds). Atlas: `inverse-wishart-spectral-moment`
(helper). Proof: Stirling's lower bound for `(x+1)!`, concavity of `log`, and the integer check.
Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.tw_inverse_moment_numeric`.

signature:

signature:

doc:
**Deviation of the extreme singular values.** For an `N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `G`

Atlas: `extreme-singular-values-deviation`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.extreme_singular_values_deviation`.

signature:
NLAlib.one_sub_two_mul_mul_specNorm_le_iSup {N n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (I : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (hI : ∀ t ∈ I, ‖t.2‖ = 1)
  (hcov :
    ∀ (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)),
      ‖u‖ = 1 → ‖v‖ = 1 → ∃ t ∈ I, ‖u - t.1‖ ≤ ε ∧ ‖v - t.2‖ ≤ ε) :
  (1 - 2 * ε) * NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ ⨆ t, ∑ i, ∑ j, (↑t).2.ofLp i * A i j * (↑t).1.ofLp j
name: NLAlib.one_sub_two_mul_mul_specNorm_le_iSup
doc:
Net argument for the spectral norm: if every pair of unit vectors `(u, v)` is `ε`-close to a
pair in the finite set `I` (whose second components are unit vectors), then
`(1 - 2ε)‖A‖₂ ≤ max_{(u,v) ∈ I} ⟨v, A u⟩`. Standard (Vershynin 2012, Lemma 5.4 in this form).
Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.gordon_upper` (helper `gu_net_bound`).
Atlas `norm-lipschitz` (helper of `gordon`, `spectral-second-moment`).

signature:
NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun g => g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g))
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => ∑ j, x j ^ 2)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Law of the residual of a Gaussian row.** Let `H` be a fixed `n × k` real matrix of rank
`n` and `g` a standard Gaussian vector in `ℝᵏ`. The squared distance from `g` to the row space of
`H`, `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g)`, has the `χ²_{k-n}` law (the law of `∑ⱼ Xⱼ²`,
`X ~ N(0, I_{k-n})`).

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean`
(helper). Proof ported from the Prove2me solution `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law`
(orthonormal basis of `ker H` and the block law `gaussianMatrix_map_block`, atlas
`block-law-indep`).

`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then

`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`
are arbitrary.

NLAlib.slepian_inequality.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {Ω' : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (Y : ι → Ω' → ℝ)
  (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => X t ω) P)
  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0) (hvar : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ^ 2 ∂P = ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ^ 2 ∂Q)

doc:

processes indexed by a finite set, with equal variances `𝔼 Xₜ² = 𝔼 Yₜ²` and dominated
increments `𝔼 (Xₛ - Xₜ)² ≤ 𝔼 (Yₛ - Yₜ)²`. Then for every `τ`,
`P(τ < maxₜ Xₜ) ≤ Q(τ < maxₜ Yₜ)`.

signature:

      ∑ j,
        ∑ k,
          ∑ l,
            A i j * A k l *
              (((((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if k = l then 1 else 0) +
                    (if i = k then 1 else 0) * if j = l then 1 else 0) +
                  (if i = l then 1 else 0) * if j = k then 1 else 0) +
                (m₄ - 3) * (((if i = j then 1 else 0) * if i = k then 1 else 0) * if i = l then 1 else 0)) =

`∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl (δ_ij δ_kl + δ_ik δ_jl + δ_il δ_jk + (m₄ − 3) δ_ijkl)
  = (tr A)² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`.
Atlas: `hutchinson-variance` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.variance_quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω)) μ =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_quadForm
doc:
**Variance of Hutchinson's estimator** (general form). If the coordinates of `z` are
independent, centred, of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄ = 𝔼[z_i⁴]`, then
`Var[zᵀ A z] = ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²` (mathematically the same as
`∑_{i≠j} (A_ij² + A_ij A_ji) + (m₄ − 1) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`; that form is not stated separately).
Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`] (Rademacher case); Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`],
Lem 5 (Gaussian), Lem 6 (Rademacher). Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.
Deviation: no symmetry of `A` assumed; general fourth moment `m₄` (`m₄ = 1` Rademacher,
`m₄ = 3` Gaussian).
